etaRequired.explainerBody: An ETA isn't a full visa — it's a short online form you complete before you fly, usually approved within minutes and linked electronically to your passport. You still apply before you travel, just not through a consulate.

US.eyebrow: Travel Guide for United States Passport Holders
US.heading: What US Passport Holders Should Know Before Traveling

howItVaries.title: How Requirements Vary by Destination
howItVaries.body: Not every destination treats a US passport the same way. Some countries let you arrive with no paperwork at all beyond your passport. Others ask for a short electronic authorization completed online before you fly — still no consulate visit, just a quick form. A smaller number require a full visa application submitted in advance. Search any destination above to see exactly which category it falls into.

whatYouNeed.title: What You'll Typically Need
whatYouNeed.body: Regardless of destination, a few things stay constant: a passport valid well beyond your planned return date, proof of onward or return travel, and evidence you can support yourself during the trip. Destinations requiring an ETA or visa will ask for a bit more — we'll show you exactly what once you search.

howWeHelp.title: Applying Through Visa Expeditor
howWeHelp.body: Once you know what's required, we handle the parts that usually eat up an afternoon — forms filled out correctly the first time, reviewed by former visa officers before anything is submitted, with real-time tracking from submission to delivery.

overview: Mexico draws more international visitors than almost anywhere else in the Americas, and the range is part of the appeal — colonial cities with centuries of layered history, Caribbean and Pacific coastlines, desert and jungle, all within a few hours of each other.

For most Western passport holders, entry is refreshingly simple: no advance visa application, just a valid passport and the standard tourist paperwork issued on arrival. That simplicity is exactly why it remains one of the most-visited countries in the world year after year.

overview: France is consistently the most-visited country on Earth by international arrivals, and Paris alone accounts for only part of the draw — the French Riviera, the châteaux of the Loire Valley, and the wine regions of Bordeaux and Burgundy all pull their own steady stream of travelers.

As part of the Schengen Area, France's entry rules are shared with 26 other European countries — a single visa-free allowance covers short stays across the whole zone, not just France, which is worth knowing if a trip spans multiple countries.
